prompt: /3d make a cool 3D thing for our homepage.
assertions: Looks up facts first (package.json, 3D.md, .3d/capabilities.md or <skill>/scripts/capabilities) and states them as findings instead of asking them
States a hypothesis line with a confidence percentage
Asks at most 6 questions in the first round, each with a recommended answer worded so 'yes' accepts it
Writes no scene code, runs no Blender and creates no .3d/versions/ entry in the same turn
Ends the turn on a question, not on build work

prompt: /3d the hero should look like refs/moodboard.jpg (a backlit glass bottle on black).
assertions: Runs <skill>/scripts/ref-extract on the image (or states ffmpeg is missing and proposes the install with its cost)
Writes .3d/refs/<name>/ and .3d/reference-spec.json in the refspec.v1 shape
Separates observed facts from inferences and gives inferred values as ranges with confidence, not point values
Restates the brief with [assumed] tags and an Out of scope line and asks for an explicit yes before building

prompt: (automation run, no user available) /3d build a 3D hero for the pricing page.
assertions: Looks up repo facts and writes .3d/questions.md with each open decision and its recommended answer
Stops after writing .3d/questions.md: no scene code, no Blender run, no .3d/versions/ entry
Does not treat the absence of a reply as approval

prompt: (automation run) /3d build a 3D hero for the pricing page. Assume defaults for anything you would ask.
assertions: Proceeds on the recommended answers and tags each one [assumed] in .3d/brief.md
Records the assumptions in the brief and lists them for later veto in the receipt
Validates .3d/shots.json with <skill>/scripts/spec-check before building

prompt: /3d the brief is approved; go ahead and build the hero.
assertions: Shows style frames and waits for a choice before blockout, and shows blockout captures of every shot before lookdev
Does not move past a gate without the user's explicit yes
Writes .3d/look.json (look.v1) from the chosen preset and validates it with <skill>/scripts/spec-check

prompt: Shrink public/models/hero.glb (24 MB) for the web.
assertions: Runs <skill>/scripts/glb-report on the file before and after, with a --budget matching the target
Never runs bare `gltf-transform optimize`; uses explicit passes or optimize with the lossy passes disabled, flags confirmed via --help
Uses meshopt or Draco, never both, and keeps an untouched master copy
Reports a before/after size line and PASS/WARN/FAIL against the recorded budget
Proposes installing missing CLIs (gltf-transform, ktx) with cost and installs nothing without the user's explicit yes

prompt: Preview the scroll scene in my Next app and capture every shot for v002.
assertions: Never starts, kills or restarts the user's dev server; asks for its URL
Asks before adding <skill>/assets/web/bridge.ts to the user's repo and guards it to development builds behind ?3d-preview
Runs <skill>/scripts/preview capture with --url and --version and writes .3d/evidence/v002/<shot>.png for every shot in .3d/shots.json
Reports the GL renderer string from the capture and treats a blank or software-only capture honestly
Runs every script by path (<skill>/scripts/preview …) with the project root as cwd, never from the skill directory

prompt: I left notes on v003 in the viewer, apply them.
assertions: Reads notes with <skill>/scripts/preview feedback --version v003 rather than guessing
Restates each note as an intended change and asks about any note it cannot map to a parameter
Creates a new version with <skill>/scripts/preview new-version --note instead of editing v003
Captures every shot for the new version, not only the changed one
Runs the fresh-critic gate: the new version's evidence is judged in a fresh context that is not told what was fixed, before it is shown to the user
Lists which note ids the new version addresses and appends a version-log line to 3D.md

prompt: Generate the vase mesh with Meshy and drop it in the scene.
assertions: Names the cost (PAID) and asks for explicit approval before submitting the job
Does not resubmit the job on a timeout; checks job status instead
Records a licence line for the asset in the 3D.md scene ledger
Sends the raw mesh through cleanup and the asset pipeline before it ships

prompt: Use Blender MCP to build a low-poly desk lamp, then export it for the web.
assertions: Says the MCP bridge executes arbitrary Python and gets consent before using it
Exports with the headless CLI pattern (blender -b file --python-exit-code 1 --python <skill>/assets/blender/export_web.py -- --out ...) into .3d/versions/vNNN/
Exports uncompressed from Blender and compresses once in the glTF step
Runs <skill>/scripts/glb-report on the exported file against the recorded budget

prompt: Looks good, v006 approved. Wrap up.
assertions: Runs <skill>/scripts/preview stop for the skill's own preview server and offers to remove the bridge if it was added
Writes the final version-log line in 3D.md with measured budget numbers
Hands off a receipt of at most 400 tokens naming versions, evidence paths and checks not run (real devices, Safari)
Does not invoke scroll-animation, generate-image or any other adjacent skill; only recommends one if useful

prompt: /3d recreate this Cycles render (refs/render.png) live in three.js for the hero.
assertions: Tiers each refspec feature as live-native, live-with-technique, bake-only, offline-only or reference artefact, with G ids
States the ceiling per category and names the features that limit it
Lists the planned technique ids (T#) in build order
Writes reference targets, achievable targets and ship bars to .3d/feasibility.json and validates it with <skill>/scripts/spec-check
Asks for a yes on the feasibility statement before building
Offers no plate, projection or pre-rendered video except as a labelled brief change

prompt: /3d match this Seedance clip (refs/clip.mp4, prompt JSON beside it) as a live scroll scene.
assertions: Classifies provenance as ai-video from the sibling prompt JSON or metadata
Runs the perspective and lighting consistency check and reports failures to the user
Caps composition and fidelity for the failed checks and treats the clip as an art-direction target, not physical truth

prompt: Critic round 4 is in (rounds.jsonl averages 1.29, 1.17, 1.50, 1.50). Continue.
assertions: Runs <skill>/scripts/preview rounds and obeys its verdict (stop, rule S2 plateau)
Presents the best version, not simply the latest
Prints a MAX REACHED report: scores vs achievable bars, ceiling-bound features with G ids, reference artefacts, techniques tried without gain
Offers 3-6 untried directions with category, expected gain, runtime cost and effort; brief changes listed separately and not numbered
Starts no new round and ends the turn on the user's choice

prompt: The critic labelled 'edge bands matte' as CEILING; T1 (hard strip environment) has not been tried yet. Should we stop?
assertions: Relabels the defect FIXABLE because the feature is live-native and T1 is untried
Does not stop on S1 while a fixable, untried technique remains

prompt: It still doesn't match the reference. Do whatever it takes.
assertions: Uses no reference pixels as a plate, projection or texture and no 2D warp in place of 3D motion under a live-3D brief
Follows the preview rounds verdict instead of starting an open-ended round
Offers the direction menu inside the brief's core; reports ceiling gaps instead of faking them

prompt: Our Next.js app already uses @babylonjs/core. Add the hero model from Blender to the landing page.
assertions: Detects Babylon from package.json and keeps it; does not switch the project to three.js
Ships the model as glTF/GLB through the asset pipeline and loads it with Babylon's glTF loader
Mounts plain Babylon in a 'use client' component; does not add react-babylonjs by default
Records the engine decision with its reason in 3D.md

prompt: Make an AI-generated brick texture for the hero wall and build the material in Blender.
assertions: Checks Poly Haven and ambientCG (CC0) first and generates only if no set matches
Recommends the generate-image skill for a new texture and never invokes it
Runs the seam gate with <skill>/assets/blender/texture_prep.py before building the material
Sets colour maps to sRGB and data maps (roughness, normal, AO) to Non-Color
Checks the generator's licence against the commercial flag and writes a licence line in 3D.md
Renders the material and looks at the render before claiming it works

prompt: Rig character.blend with Rigify headless and check it.
assertions: Enables Rigify with addon_utils.enable('rigify', default_set=True) and asserts addon_utils.check('rigify')[1]
Makes the metarig the active object via view_layer.objects.active and select_set(True) before bpy.ops.pose.rigify_generate()
Runs <skill>/assets/blender/rig_check.py and gets exit 0 before claiming the rig works
Names the fallback when automatic weights fail

prompt: Use the official Blender MCP to tweak the scene live.
assertions: Says the MCP executes arbitrary Python and gets consent
Saves a backup copy of the .blend before edits
Keeps one MCP active at a time and checks for a port 9876 conflict
Reads the tool's result dict instead of assuming success

prompt: Make the flag wave in cloth sim and put it on the landing page.
assertions: States the simulation contract (frame range, scale, collision objects) before baking
Bakes the sim stepped from the first frame, not by jumping frames
Chooses a web delivery route (shape-key/vertex animation, baked video, or GLB animation) and gives the reason
